name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,589

clue.text: Converting our assets and income into something very welcome

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so the words that follow get rebuilt into a new phrase

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder
also taken letter for letter; 'and' simply joins it to the rest of the fodder

explanation.surface: An accountant cheerfully turning a family's savings and earnings into a windfall.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial surface makes 'converting' look like cashing in; really it rearranges OUR ASSETS plus INCOME into MUSIC TO ONE'S EARS.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes news or words that someone is very pleased to hear, so it names anything warmly received.

clue.text: Innumerable milk suppliers having no space, becoming upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, to upset is to turn upside down, so what remains is read from the bottom up

blocks.note: the people who run dairies and supply milk
an en is a printer's space, half the width of an em

explanation.surface: Countless dairy farmers squeezed for room and growing distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: DAIRYMEN loses EN, the printer's space, leaving DAIRYM, which reads upwards as MYRIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Myriad works as an adjective meaning countless or too many to count, exactly the sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Songsmith, essentially mischievous and egocentric

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letter of the songwriter is kept

blocks.note: the middle letter: the fifth of nine sits dead centre
elves are proverbially impish, so elfish means mischievous

explanation.surface: A description of a songwriter who is at heart a prankster and full of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma tempts you to take 'Songsmith' whole as a definition, but only its central S is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person concerned chiefly with their own interests and wishes, making them close synonyms.

clue.text: Dog food

blocks.note: a fluffy Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue
informal word for grub or a meal

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it asks for pet food; split it and each word is its own definition of the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a Chinese breed of dog with a blue-black tongue; the other is slang for something to eat.

clue.text: Eye surgery to itch from time to time

indicators.note: something done only at intervals, so letters are taken every other place along the phrase

blocks.note: short for operation
first, third and fifth letters of the two words run together

explanation.surface: A patient recovering from eye surgery whose healing wound itches now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters run across both words 'to itch', taking T, I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: An optic is a colloquial and technical term for the organ of sight, and as an adjective means relating to vision.

clue.text: Friend supports new planet being discovered, of course

indicators.note: to dis-cover is to strip away the covering
in a down clue a supporter stands underneath

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
SATURN with its first and last letters removed
an ally is a friend or partner

explanation.surface: An astronomer's colleague backing the discovery of a new planet, as you would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's discovery of a planet is really SATURN being uncovered to ATUR; N and ALLY sandwich it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are sentence adverbs used to say that something is obvious or only to be expected.

clue.text: Assist performer indirectly

blocks.note: to second is to back or support, as a second does in a duel or boxing
a hand is a worker or one who does a job, as in farmhand or old hand

explanation.surface: Helping a stage performer in a roundabout way from the wings.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adverb: news heard second-hand reaches you through someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand describes information received through an intermediary rather than from its original source, which matches indirectly.

clue.text: Pilot coming from Malaga, via Torremolinos

indicators.note: the answer emerges out of the place names that follow, straddling their boundary

blocks.note: last letter of the first town, the whole of 'via', and the start of the resort

explanation.surface: A holiday flight route along Spain's Costa del Sol from Malaga through Torremolinos.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the comma: malagA VIA TORremolinos hides the answer, and 'via' is doing its best to look like a mere route word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is someone who flies aircraft, and aviator is the somewhat old-fashioned word for exactly that person.

clue.text: Back head abandoning exam, it's most rigorous

blocks.note: the stern is the back of a ship
TEST without its first letter

explanation.surface: A schoolchild quitting an exam, told it is the toughest one going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back head' looks like a phrase about the back of the skull; split it, 'Back' is the stern and 'head' belongs with the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of stern, meaning strictest or most severe, lines up with the superlative in the clue.

clue.text: List of names not considered for product launch

blocks.note: a roll is a register, as in a roll call
out of the question, ruled out

explanation.surface: A marketing team drawing up a shortlist of names and rejecting some for a new product.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests brand names being rejected; in fact the list and the rejection simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollout is the business term for introducing a new product or service to market in stages.

clue.text: Reportedly what a roofer may do that's perceptible by touch

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth

blocks.note: a roofer might tack down a tile

explanation.surface: A roofer's task described as something you can feel with your hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Tack tile, said quickly, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile describes things that can be felt with the fingers or relate to the sense of touch.

clue.text: Bitter, bitter having leaked runs

blocks.note: acrid means sharp and bitter
cricket scoring abbreviation

explanation.surface: Beer from a leaking barrel that has run out, leaving the drinker sour.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word looks like a typo; the first is the definition, the second the ACRID that loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid remarks are sharp and sour in tone, the same resentful sense as a bitter one.

clue.text: Bill caught sound of caller on mobile briefly, Stanley perhaps?

definitions.note: Accrington Stanley is the club; the town's name comes before Stanley

blocks.note: short for account, which is a bill
cricket scorecard abbreviation
RINGTONE, what plays when someone calls, cut short

explanation.surface: A man called Bill catching a phone's ringing briefly, maybe while out with a friend called Stanley.
explanation.walkthrough: Accrington Stanley is a Lancashire football club, famous in Britain from an old milk advert; the question mark admits the town is only part of the club's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley is the second half of the club name Accrington Stanley, so the town completes the pairing as a clue by example.

clue.text: Influence criminal case due to begin in French city

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or bent

blocks.note: anagram fodder
its opening letter
the capital of Lorraine in north-east France

explanation.surface: A criminal trial about to open in France that everyone hopes to sway.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom story hides three separate jobs: 'criminal' is an anagram signal, 'due to begin' gives one letter, and Nancy is a city in Lorraine, north-east France.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendancy means dominance or controlling power over others, which is the kind of sway meant by influence.

clue.text: Concrete is child's play to mix, vacuous lad conceded

indicators.note: what is conceded is given up, so those two letters are surrendered from the phrase
mixing jumbles the remaining letters together

blocks.note: the phrase letter for letter
LAD emptied of its middle

explanation.surface: A builder boasting that mixing concrete is easy, while an empty-headed young worker admits defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' wants to be the building material; it is the adjective. Take one L and the D out of CHILDSPLAY, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something real and tangible that exists in material form rather than being abstract.

clue.text: Garlic oil's cooked, producing a little smoke

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these words are worked into a new shape

blocks.note: the letters of the two words; the 's joins them to 'cooked'

explanation.surface: A cook frying garlic in oil so that the pan gives off a wisp of smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen smoke is the trick; the 's reads as 'is' before 'cooked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarillo is a small thin cigar, so it is literally a small thing to smoke.

clue.text: Home Secretary defends weapon that causes injury

indicators.note: to defend something is to surround and shield it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for the UK government minister
arms are weapons

explanation.surface: A government minister defending the legality of a dangerous weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Secretary is the British cabinet minister responsible for policing and security, which makes the political surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: To harm someone is to hurt or damage them, and the third-person verb matches the clue phrase.

clue.text: Happen to block line for drinks, we hear, in party

indicators.note: we hear it rather than see it

blocks.note: as in 'let it be', meaning let it happen
the queue at a bar, with queue said as the letter Q or cue

explanation.surface: Someone pushing into the drinks queue at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: A queue is the British word for a waiting line, and 'happen' gives its letters through 'let it be'.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is an outdoor social gathering where food is grilled, so it is a kind of party.

clue.text: Golfer reflected on sloth somewhere in church

indicators.note: a mirror image is back to front
in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

blocks.note: the ai is the three-toed sloth, a crossword favourite
Ernie Els, the South African golfer

explanation.surface: A golfer reflecting in church on the sin of sloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like the deadly sin, fitting the church; here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is the passageway between the pews of a church, so it is one particular place inside it.

clue.text: America imprisoning philosopher? Conversely, it could be baloney over there

definitions.text: it could be baloney over there

indicators.note: a prison surrounds its inmate, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a sage is a wise thinker
standard abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A question of whether an imprisoned philosopher's talk in America is just nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baloney' wants to mean nonsense; it is the American spelling of bologna, the sausage, hence 'over there'.
explanation.definitionFit: Baloney is a large smoked American sausage, so it serves as one example of the general class of meat product.

clue.text: South American chap, 29, main lessee

indicators.note: the answer at 29 across means at regular intervals, so only every other letter is taken

blocks.note: a guy is a man
second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A man from South America aged twenty-nine who is the principal tenant of a property.
explanation.walkthrough: The number looks like an age; it is a cross-reference to EVERY NOW AND THEN, telling you to pick alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyana is a country on the northern coast of that continent, and its adjective describes a person from there.

clue.text: Leaves hospital after cycle ride leads to accidental crash

indicators.note: the leading letters are the opening ones of the two words that follow

blocks.note: a spin is a short ride out
initial letters of both words
map and road-sign abbreviation

explanation.surface: A cyclist discharged from hospital after a bike ride ended in a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb about quitting hospital; it is the plural noun, the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable eaten for its dark edible foliage, so it is a mass of leaves.

clue.text: Tory knight, possibly a fraudster

blocks.note: short for Conservative, the British party whose members are called Tories
a knight is one example of a chessman

explanation.surface: A knighted Conservative politician suspected of fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight' suggests a title like Sir; in the wordplay it is a chess piece, and 'possibly' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A con man is a swindler who wins people's trust in order to cheat them, which is what a fraudster does.

clue.text: Sure sign revealing a batsman's ambitions?

blocks.note: as in 'bound to happen'
a sign of the zodiac, the ram

explanation.surface: An obvious clue to what a cricketer is hoping for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sure sign' reads as one idiom; it splits into two pieces. In cricket a boundary is a shot reaching the edge of the field, scoring four or six.
explanation.definitionFit: Every batter hopes to hit balls to the rope for four or six runs, so these scoring shots are what a batsman aims for.

clue.text: Run more than usual

blocks.note: in cricket a run not scored off the bat, such as a bye or wide
additional, beyond the normal amount

explanation.surface: An instruction to jog further than normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a verb; it is a cricket noun. An extra is a run credited to the batting side from a bowling or fielding error.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra as an adjective means additional or beyond the normal amount; as a cricket noun it is a run not off the bat.

clue.text: Love going around over alternative to carpet

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, and nil is zero
cricket scorecard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone in love going round a room thinking about flooring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' tempts you to take the letter O; here it is NIL, and the O comes from 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lino, short for linoleum, is a hard floor covering often laid instead of rugs or fitted flooring.

clue.text: Slip by youngster carrying pole

indicators.note: in a down clue what is carried rides on top

blocks.note: the South Pole, abbreviated
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A child carrying a long pole losing their footing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a stick; it is a compass point, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is a sliding loss of grip, as a car or foot does on ice, just like a slip.

clue.text: Sound name adopted by fashion designer

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
Coco Chanel, the French couturier

explanation.surface: A strong brand name taken on by a fashion house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is set up as an adjective meaning solid; it is the noun for a stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow stretch of sea between two landmasses, which is also what a channel is.

clue.text: Prepare to fire male working at IKEA previously

indicators.note: the letters are put to work and so moved about into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A manager about to sack a man who used to work at the furniture store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like dismissal from the job; it means shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: To take aim is to point a gun at a target just before shooting, which is how one readies to fire.

clue.text: New oven Henry wanted periodically

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the following words appear in fresh order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, fifteen letters

explanation.surface: A man called Henry who has wanted a new cooker from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' reads as describing the oven; it is the signal to rearrange everything after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions mean occasionally, at irregular intervals, rather than all the time.
